THE ONE YOU’VE ALL BEEN WAITING FOR: COLLAGEN CHAT (Girl Science Edition) 🩷 First up, collagen is important. It’s what keeps your skin bouncy, joints cushioned, and tissues strong. Your body makes collagen, but rom your mid-20s, that production starts to dip – and drops faster post-menopause thanks to hormonal changes. DO YOU NEED TO TAKE A COLLAGEN SUPPLEMENT? Collagen supplements don’t “top up” your collagen directly. They’re broken down into small peptides that signal your body to make more, but only if your body’s in the right state to respond. That generally comes from you sleeping well, eating a balanced diet with enough protein and managing your stress, Without those foundations, the signal’s weak – and your collagen powder probably won’t do much. Where collagen actually delivers: 💞Joints: Hydrolysed or type II collagen can help reduce joint pain and slow cartilage breakdown (especially if osteoarthritis runs in your family). 🌟Skin: Evidence is mixed. High-quality, independent studies show minimal benefit for elasticity or hydration. 💅Hair & nails: Not much science here yet. Takehome message: collagen can support you, but it’s not a miracle. Focus on your foundations first – balanced nutrition, sleep, and stress management – and collagen becomes the cherry on top, not the whole sundae 🍒 #collagen #collagenforwomen #girlscience #womenshealth #hormonehealth

Here's the simple science behind the old Appalachian "collagen boost" recipe: 🍊 Orange Juice (Vitamin C) Vitamin C is one of the most important nutrients for collagen production. Your body uses vitamin C to help link together the amino acids that form collagen fibers. Without enough vitamin C, your body can't efficiently make or repair collagen. 🍮 Jell-O (Gelatin) Gelatin is basically cooked-down collagen from animal connective tissues. When you eat gelatin, it provides amino acids☆especially glycine, proline, and hydroxyproline☆which are the building blocks your body uses to make its own collagen. 🥥 Coconut Oil Coconut oil doesn't contain collagen and doesn't directly create collagen. However, it provides fats that support overall skin health and may help reduce dryness and support the skin barrier. Think of it as supporting healthy skin rather than supplying collagen itself. How They Work Together Jell-O/gelatin supplies the raw materials (amino acids). Orange juice supplies the vitamin C needed to build collagen. Coconut oil helps support skin health and moisture. That's why old-timers often paired gelatin with a source of vitamin C. The combination gives your body both the building blocks and one of the key nutrients needed for collagen production. A lot of folks today are basically doing the same thing with expensive collagen powders and vitamin C supplements. Granny was just doing it with Jell-O and orange juice. 😊 One thing to keep in mind: eating gelatin or collagen doesn't automatically become collagen in your skin. Your body breaks it down into amino acids first and then uses those building blocks wherever they're needed. But research does suggest that collagen peptides and gelatin can support collagen production when combined with a healthy diet and adequate vitamin C. #mountainwisdom #collagenboost  #appalachianmagic
